place_info.title: Iron Works Barbecue
place_info.address: 100 Red River St, Austin, TX 78701, United States

reviews.snippet:
Came into this spot because average rating was decent and we've been to all the top 6-7 spots in the immediate Austin area already. Figured try something new and see why so many 5 star ratings. Around 4:45pm on a Friday...not a soul in sight.

This was barely 1 star for us. Each meat was wrong. Brisket dry, zero fat. Rib so oily and chewy could barely pull off the bone. Turkey was over smoked. Sausage was run of the mill...filling was reminiscent of just a hot dog fill. Every side lacked flavor and freshness. Green beans mushy, slaw so runny it was dripping, bbq beans we're tasteless. Not sure why add the pickles and onions it added nothing to the plates. The only decent side was creamed corn as it had some flavor. All this was $80+ dollars with a beer.

The pro is the spot is really neat inside and location is right downtown Austin. Our assumption after eating here is that the 5-star ratings are not for the food but atmosphere, location, and was probably a great spot for bbq back in the day? I guess to each there own and try if you want.

The takeout order was less than acceptable bbq. The meat was over cooked, the beans were tasteless and the Mac and cheese had a hair in it.

reviews.snippet:
I chose Iron Works BBQ for a team dinner with my boss and several colleagues based on its reputation and reviews, and unfortunately it turned out to be a disappointing experience.

The staff was friendly, but there were warning signs from the start. We arrived around 6:00 PM and were the only customers in the restaurant. Despite having a group of eight and an otherwise empty dining room, we were seated outside in 100-degree heat with limited airflow from a few weak fans. It made for a very uncomfortable dining experience, especially when there appeared to be plenty of indoor seating available.

The ordering process was also surprisingly slow for a larger group. Orders are taken one at a time, with a single employee carving and serving the meat, creating a bottleneck that doesn't work well when several people are trying to order together.

As for the food, it simply didn't live up to the restaurant's reputation. The ribs were fatty and lacked tenderness. The brisket was dry. The sides—including the beans and mac and cheese—were bland and forgettable. Nothing we ordered stood out in a positive way.

What made the experience particularly disappointing was that I had specifically recommended Iron Works to my coworkers based on the strong reviews I'd seen. The next morning, several of us were discussing where we could have gone for truly great Texas barbecue instead.

For comparison, I later stopped at Salt Lick BBQ in the Austin airport and found the food to be dramatically better across the board.

Given the quality of the food, the uncomfortable seating arrangement, and the overall experience, I don't feel Iron Works justifies its rating or its prices. I can't recommend it based on my visit.

reviews.snippet:
Visited on a Friday night and was surprised the place wasn’t full for a BBQ restaurant. Unfortunately, the food explained why.

The baked beans looked and tasted like they came straight out of a can. The bread was being taken right out of the plastic bag, which makes it obvious there’s no real effort in the food. The mac and cheese looked microwaved, honestly, Kraft’s version tastes better. And the meat was completely tasteless, which is the biggest disappointment for a BBQ spot.

Save your time and money and go somewhere else.
To the owners: please cook with love so it shows in the food. Very disappointed.

reviews.snippet: Got the sampler and sausage was average, brisket was not very flavorful and if it cooked longer at low heat the fat would have rendered more. Corn average. No love in the meal. When I ordered they didn’t even ask if I wanted pork or beef ribs and gave us 2 plates of beef. This restaurant is placed perfectly downtown but they have no pride in the food. So much potential here.

reviews.snippet: While traveling with family we ate supper here. Our hotel recommended this bbq restaurant. The atmosphere is unique, it’s an old blacksmith shop. The bbq was subpar, very small servings - the beans tasted “off” - not the beans we are used to. I didn’t see any “locals” so I’m thinking the surrounding hotels just suggest the closest bbq. Over $25 (to include tax) for each small styrofoam white plate with plastic forks.
